about: Two comparisons and no search. `b`'s demand sits under `a`'s, and
`a`'s limit under `b`'s — the direction reverses between the two
marks, and an implementation that compares both the same way passes
the reflexive cases and fails the rest.
A statement nothing can satisfy entails everything, which is the last
case and the one nobody thinks to write.

coverage.criterion: reflexive, strictly narrower each way, incomparable, and an unsatisfiable statement on both sides
coverage.why: one scale only; reflexivity and transitivity over every pair are asserted in the unit tests

cases.name: wider ceiling does not entail narrower
lower floor does not entail higher
